# Charlotta

## Overview

- **Age:** Teenager (fourteen to sixteen in earlier volumes, older in volume 4)  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v3 c23 P7](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0007)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v3 c23 P7](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0007)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v4 c3 P9](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0009), [v4 c3 P38](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0038)</sub>
- **Role:** Handmaiden / Housekeeper  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c27 P43](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0043)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Charlotta the Fourth  <sub>[v2 c21 P46](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0046), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

## Appearance

Charlotta has a freckled face, a snub nose, and a exceptionally wide mouth and smile. In her earlier years, she tied her hair into two crinkly plaits adorned with prominent blue ribbon bows. As she grew into young ladyhood, she discarded the blue bows in favor of styling her hair into an enormous pompadour.

_Sources: [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c27 P47](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0047), [v2 c30 P27](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0027), [v3 c23 P7](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0007), [v4 c3 P37](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0037)_

## Personality

Charlotta is an energetic, loyal, and warm-hearted girl who deeply adores her mistress, Miss Lavendar, and Anne Shirley. She is hardworking, dutiful, and eager to please, often skipping or flying about her household chores. Though practical, straightforward, and pragmatic about romance, she tolerates and never judges Miss Lavendar's imaginative make-believe.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P69](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0069), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c27 P43](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0043), [v2 c27 P44](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0044), [v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055), [v2 c28 P56](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0056), [v2 c30 P11](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0011)_

## History

At fourteen years old, Charlotta worked as a handmaiden for Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge. She assisted in entertaining guests such as Anne Shirley and Diana Barry, using a tin horn to trigger the famous echoes across the river. Charlotta took immense care of her mistress and worried deeply whenever Miss Lavendar appeared lonely or unwell. When Stephen Irving returned to reunite with Miss Lavendar, Charlotta helped Anne prepare the house and eagerly supported the romance. Following Miss Lavendar and Stephen Irving's wedding, Charlotta moved with them to Boston. She returned to Echo Lodge during summer vacations, where she continued to welcome Anne Shirley with affection. Later, Charlotta married an American named Tom, a bricklayer, but obtained his consent to travel back to Prince Edward Island to attend Anne Shirley's wedding.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P68](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0068), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c27 P44](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0044), [v2 c28 P48](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0048), [v2 c29 P10](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0010), [v3 c23 P1](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0001), [v3 c40 P0](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0000), [v4 c3 P38](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0038), [v4 c3 P42](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0042), [v4 c4 P16](../source/v04-c04.md#nw-v04-c04-p0016)_

## Background by volume

- Her real name is Leonora, but Miss Lavendar called her Charlotta the Fourth to avoid confusion with her older sisters who previously held the same position.  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- She is the youngest and last of the Bowman girls from her family.  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- Her sister Charlotta the First went to live in Boston, a path expected of the Bowman girls when reaching age sixteen.  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c28 P55](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0055)</sub>

## Quotes

> In this world you’ve just got to hope for the best and prepare for the worst and take whatever God sends.  <sub>[v2 c30 P16](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0016)</sub>

> When all’s said and done, Miss Shirley, ma’am, I haven’t seen any one in Boston that’s equal to you  <sub>[v3 c40 P1](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0001)</sub>

> I never did think I’d come down to marrying a Yankee, Miss Shirley, ma’am. But you never know what’s before you, and it isn’t his fault. He was born that way.  <sub>[v4 c3 P38](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0038)</sub>
